stem:
Gauri has $\triangle PQR$ with a right angle at $P$, $PQ=6$, and $PR=8$. She wants the length of $QR$.

Which claim correctly applies $a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$?

options.text: $6^{2}+8^{2}=QR^{2}$ even if angle $P$ were not a right angle.
The hypotenuse $QR$ is what creates the right angle at $P$.
$PQ$ and $PR$ are the perpendicular sides, so $6^{2}+8^{2}=QR^{2}$ and $QR=10$.

teacher.key_rationale: Right angle at P makes PQ and PR the legs and QR the hypotenuse: 36+64=100 so QR=10. Applying the relation without a right angle omits the condition. Saying the hypotenuse creates the right angle reverses the relation. Calling PQ the hypotenuse mis-identifies c.
